public_rationale: OpenAI's September 3, 2026 disclosure reports broad benchmark advances for Astra [e1]. ARC Prize's evaluation that day reports substantial progress but explains that ARC-AGI-3 has a bounded scope and that its saturation does not prove AGI [e2]. These items establish neither independently verified fulfillment of the broad capability promises by an in-scope product nor an impossibility result covering the specified methods, so the claim remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: The disclosure does not establish continuity between all essential Astra methods and methods known on February 23, 2026 [e1].
The benchmark evaluation does not establish broad, reliable, sustained human-level competence across domains [e2].
Neither evidence item supplies an impossibility result; this does not establish that no such result exists elsewhere [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The generative AI products vendors actually know how to build cannot live up to the AGI-level expectations they have sold.

statement.excerpt: And there is just no way for the product they actually know how build — as opposed to the one they fantasize about — to live up to those expectations.
statement.document_title: Turns out Generative AI was a scam

from_speaker: the product they actually know how build
to live up to those expectations
our_interpretation: Read 'those expectations' as the preceding claim's AGI-level expectations.
Read the scope as products developed through the generative-AI methods vendors demonstrably knew at publication, allowing further development of those methods.
The claim states an impossibility without a deadline. Current shortcomings alone cannot support it.
Use broad, flexible human-level cognitive competence as the ordinary capability reading, without requiring perfection.
criteria.support_condition: A compelling impossibility result establishes that the specified class of methods cannot deliver the advertised broad capabilities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying product demonstrably delivers the advertised broad capabilities, with independent verification and evidence that it falls within the claimed technical scope.

evidence.explanation: The later product is a relevant candidate counterexample, and the disclosure reports broad benchmark advances. Its high-level description does not establish that every essential method was known at publication or that the complete AGI-level promise was fulfilled.

The evaluator reports 62.7% with its standard setup and 99.9% with a provider-adapted setup, while emphasizing the benchmark's bounded scope. This is substantial progress to consider, but it does not meet the stated decisive-event rule.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent verification that a product delivers broad, flexible human-level cognitive competence, including reliable and sustained performance across domains, with technical evidence placing it within the specified methods; or a valid impossibility result covering that method class.
